findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_booking_link" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Free, instant pre-flight check for a booking URL. Classifies which booking platform a URL belongs to and tells you whether import_booking_url will accept it, WI…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_business" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Given criteria (vertical, location, capability, price band, availability window), return ranked candidate businesses from our supply network. THE NETWORK IS SMALL AND STILL MOSTLY SAMPLE DATA: entries that are not real are named [DEMO] and flagged is_demo - check that field before acting on a result" → after: "Find real businesses near a place, sorted by distance (nearest of those examined; see result.search). Data: OpenStreetMap (ODbL, (c) OSM contributors); phone, website, hours only when mapped. Coverage varies; community-mapped, NOT verified by us; source=openstreetmap rows cannot be booked. Answers w"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
